newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity rises with strong physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity rises with strong physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rose Friday with front month contracts hitting new highs on strong physical power prices, industry sources said.
"It seems to be all based on the physicals," one Houston-based electricity trader said.

As of 1240 EDT, NYMEX July Palo Verde (PV) futures were up $1.83 at $33.20 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $33.75 and a low of $32.80, while August was up 90 cents at $33.70 following trades at a new contract high of $34.00 and a low of $33.65 per MWh.

July California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up $1.00 at $24.40 following exchanges at a new contract high of $24.75 and a low of $24.25, while August was up 11 cents at $26.10 after trades in a range of $26.00-26.75 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1145 EDT an estimated total of 109 COB and 432 PV contracts had traded.
Physical power prices in the U.S. Southwest remained strong, sources said, with Monday peak, firm PV power assessed steady from Thursday discussion at $40.00-42.00 per MWh.
Monday peak, firm COB power was pegged at near $32.00 per MWh, although sources said prices fell off in later morning trade to the $20.00 and $21.00 range from $27.00-29.00 on Thursday.

Weather in the U.S. Southwest remained hot, with significant cooling demand, while temperatures in parts of southern California like Los Angeles was also warm enough to warrant some air conditioning demand, sources said.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be near normal in the northeast over the next several days to five degrees above normal in the southwest. Precipitation was expected to average above-normal over the Rocky Mountains and below-normal elsewhere.
In Phoenix, Ariz., maximum temperatures were expected to reach 105 degrees Fahrenheit on Saturday and 99 degrees on Monday, with overnight lows near 77 degrees.
In Los Angeles, maximum temperatures were expected to near 80 degrees Saturday and 76 degrees Monday with overnight lows near 62 degrees.
Futures prices at COB were said to be rising in sympathy with PV as players looked to import power from the Pacific Northwest into the Southwest.
In the Pacific Northwest, forecasts called for temperatures three degrees above normal in the southwest to five degrees above normal in the northeast over the next several days.
Precipitation was expected to average above normal over the extreme northwest sections to near to below normal elsewhere.
Portland, Oregon was expected to see a maximum temperature near 66 degrees on Saturday and 61 degrees on Monday, with overnight lows near 50 degrees.

Separately, Arizona Public Service's 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear power unit near Phoenix remained off line for repairs Friday morning despite company expectations the unit would resume electricity production Thursday.
Also, the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear power unit remained off line for refueling, and was expected to restart this weekend.

In addition to the Palo Verde and Diablo Canyon nukes, several units were expected to return to service by Monday, including a 750 MW unit at Colstrip in Montana, a 750 MW unit at Four Corners in Arizona, a 550 MW unit at Jim Bridger in Wyoming and a 400 MW unit at the Bonanza plant in Utah.
PV open interest for May 29 fell 55 to 6,273, while COB open interest fell 417 to 5,371, NYMEX said.
